profile.name: Ganesh Derkar
headline: Thoughtful code.
Useful software.
profile.intro: I’m Ganesh, a Full Stack Software Developer at Endava. I build intuitive interfaces, dependable APIs, and applications that connect the two.
bio: I’m a Full Stack Software Developer at Endava with a background in Computer Engineering from MIT Academy of Engineering. I enjoy working across the stack, from the details of a responsive interface to the structure of a backend service.

My toolkit includes React, Angular, .NET Web API, and microservices. I work with Docker and GitHub Actions for delivery, and use OpenAI and Gemini API integrations in my projects to explore practical AI features.
I’m interested in software that is easy to use and easy to maintain. Spec-driven development with Spec Kit helps me connect requirements, implementation plans, and the code that follows.

projects.title: NetflixGPT
projects.subtitle: A movie discovery experience
Find your next film
projects.description: A movie-focused web application pairing a React interface with Firebase authentication and backend services.
projects.overview: A personal project exploring the experience of discovering movies through a familiar streaming-style interface. React powers the frontend while Firebase provides the backend foundation.
highlights: Streaming-inspired interface with a responsive layout.
Sign-in experience connected to Firebase.
Reusable React components for the browsing experience.
highlights.description: Find films through AI recommendations, browse TMDB movie collections, and watch trailers in one React app.
highlights.overview: NetflixGPT brings movie discovery and trailer playback into one interface. I connected TMDB movie data with Gemini recommendations and Firebase authentication, using Redux to share application state across the browsing experience.
highlights: Browse now-playing, popular, and top-rated movies from TMDB, alongside Gemini-powered recommendations.
Open trailers from movie posters in a modal that also closes with the Escape key.
Reuse trailer-fetching logic through custom hooks and share movie data through Redux.

Food browsing, built with React
highlights.description: A responsive food delivery interface with API-driven content, client-side routing, and reusable React hooks.
highlights.overview: An exploration of a practical food ordering interface, with an emphasis on reusable components, navigation, and working with external API data.
highlights: Client-side navigation with React Router.
API integration for dynamic content.
Custom hooks that share stateful logic across components.
highlights.description: A food browsing interface with API-driven listings, page navigation, and shared React hooks.
highlights.overview: This project explores the frontend of a food delivery application. I connected external API content to reusable React components and used React Router for navigation, with custom hooks keeping shared stateful logic out of individual views.
highlights: Use React Router to move between views without a full-page reload.
Populate the interface with external API data rather than hardcoded listings.
Share stateful logic through custom hooks so components can focus on rendering.
